en.title: Polish President Turns Back Flight to Senegal After Court Chief Suspended
en.dek: President Karol Nawrocki returned to Poland after the Constitutional Tribunal suspended its president, amid protests and accusations of a coup d'état.
facts: President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane around en route to Senegal on 30 October 2026.
The Constitutional Tribunal suspended its president, Bogdan Święczkowski, on 30 October 2026.
Riot police were deployed outside the Tribunal and entered the building after incidents involving dangerous objects.
The Tribunal’s official X account described the suspension as a "coup d'état".
body: President Karol Nawrocki announced on X that he was cutting short his flight to Senegal and returning to Poland after riot police entered the Constitutional Tribunal premises. The announcement followed police entering the building after incidents involving dangerous objects. The flight was turned back on 30 October 2026.

Outside the Tribunal, supporters of the former nationalist Law and Justice party gathered to protest the suspension. They chanted slogans such as "Tusk traitor" according to an AFP journalist. Some protesters held Catholic rosaries and religious images while police guarded the building’s entrance.

The Constitutional Tribunal has been at the center of a long‑running dispute between the current parliamentary majority and the former government. President Nawrocki, an ally of the former government, had refused to swear in three of six judges nominated by parliament earlier in the year. The Tribunal’s president, Bogdan Święczkowski, had declined to allow judges elected by the current parliamentary majority to assume their duties, effectively paralyzing the institution.

Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek told journalists that he had requested the lifting of immunity for Święczkowski and his deputy, Bartłomiej Sochański. The Tribunal’s official X account described the suspension as a "coup d'état", stating that "Ms. Anna Korwin-Piotrowska is not a judge of the Constitutional Tribunal" and that "all persons participating in these actions are committing the crime of a coup d'état." The European Union had previously accused the court of being too closely aligned with the government. President Nawrocki has blocked the appointments of the current parliamentary majority to the court.
en.context: The Constitutional Tribunal has been a point of contention between Poland’s current ruling party and the former nationalist Law and Justice party. The court has ruled that Polish law takes precedence over EU law, leading to criticism from Brussels. The dispute over judge appointments has paralyzed the institution.
